reading.body:
Box has built a portfolio of integrations that let AI agents handle real-world tasks: sending physical mail, managing cloud files, accessing bank data, and exchanging secrets between agents.

These Model Context Protocol tools sit at the boundary between AI systems and the infrastructure they need to operate at scale. An AI agent that can only think cannot process a loan application or onboard an employee. It must read files, verify identity, send documents, and maintain audit trails. Box's integrations bridge this gap by giving agents standardized access to storage, communication channels, and cross-agent coordination. The company's own AI product focuses on enterprise content, but this MCP registry strategy positions it as an operational layer for agentic workflows, where the binding constraint shifts from model capability to the ability to act on real data and systems.

What these integrations do not show is compute or power consumption. They are software abstractions that assume infrastructure exists elsewhere. They do show that AI scaling now depends not only on larger models and more training compute, but on standardized ways for agents to access the human-world interfaces they need to do work. For enterprises, this means the grid constraint on AI is mediated through the systems that connect agents to email, filesystems, banks, and each other.

profile_text.body:
Box is a public company headquartered in Redwood City, California, providing intelligent content management, workflow, and collaboration software. Founded in 2005, Box describes its platform as one that helps teams access, share, edit, and co-create content while automating workflows and protecting sensitive data. The company reported revenue of $1,177,253,000 for the fiscal year ending January 31, 2026.

Box offers Box AI, an enterprise content AI product that integrates metadata management, governance, compliance, and retention policies. According to the company, Box AI seamlessly connects leading AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google to provide real-time summaries, analysis, and recommendations on unstructured data. The platform includes workflow automation with a drag-and-drop builder, AI-driven security with deep learning-based malware detection, and compliance tools for GDPR, HIPAA, and FINRA requirements. Box also offers AI-driven e-signature capabilities and Box AI Studio for developers to customize agents and build agentic experiences.

Beyond its core products, Box is registered in the Model Context Protocol registry with eight MCP servers, including tools for email handling, file storage access, Dropbox integration, and physical mail APIs designed to enable AI agents to interact with various enterprise systems and data sources.
